newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Power NZ says too soon to comment on offer.
newsitem.headline: Power NZ says too soon to comment on offer.

text.p: Power New Zealand Ltd said on Thursday it intended to appoint merchant bankers Bancorp Advisory Services to carry out an independent appraisal report on the offer for its shares by Utilicorp NZ and Mercury Energy. Power NZ Chairman Don Stanley, said that in the absence of detailed information from the joint venture partners it was inappropriate at this stage for the Board to make any comment on the proposed offer, which was still subject to Overseas Investment Commission and Commerce Commission approvals.
Utilicorp NZ, a unit of Kansas-based Utilicorp United Inc, and unlisted Mercury on Tuesday said they would form a joint venture to hold their respective Power NZ shareholdings.
The deal ended a long-running and bitter battle for control of Power New Zealand between its two largest shareholders.
PNZ's Stanley said it could be some time before the approvals for the joint venture were obtained.
"In the interim, the board and management will continue to operate the business in the best interests of the company and all its shareholders," he said.
